 Order

This Miscellaneous Appeal is filed by the Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved of award dated 23.04.2012, passed by learned II Addl. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Waraseoni, District Balaghat (M.P.), in Claim Case No.26/2011, whereby,

entities.text: II Addl. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Waraseoni
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: learned
Claims Tribunal has allowed the claim and granted compensation in favour of the claimants.

2. A perusal of the grounds of appeal reveal that according to the appellant, accident took place on 20.03.2011, intimation was given to the Police Station on 26.03.2011, but FIR was lodged on 08.05.2011 after 19 days of the incident falsely implicating the motor cycle which was insured with the present appellant.

3. In the grounds of appeal, it is mentioned that there is a collusion between the claimants and the respondent No.5, who appeared in the witness box and said everything in favour of claimants and,
therefore, the impugned award is vitiated.
4. Though, nobody is appearing on behalf of claimants, I have carefully perused the record, which is available.
5. FIR was recorded on 08.05.2011, on the basis of the intimation which was received by the Police Station on 26.03.2011, at 20:10 hours.
However, there is a mention of entry in Rojnamcha bearing No.289 at 7:00 hours.

In this FIR Ex.A/1, there is a mention of Merg intimation and it is mentioned that accident took place on 20.03.2011 at about 3-4 P.M. when red colour motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-50MB/9800, came driven rashly and negligently had caused accident causing grievous injuries to injured Shravan Gour, who died while under treatment.
6. Police had investigated the matter and filed a charge sheet against the owner-driver of the said motorcycle, which is insured with the appellant.

7. I have gone through the evidence as was adduced by the witness Maya Bhalvi, Prakash Patle and also that given by the owner-driver of the motorcycle, namely, Mahendra Kirnapure, who had accepted the fatum of accident.
There is no contradiction in their cross-examination.

Interestedly,

2 insurance Company did not bother to examine any independent witness including their Investigating Officer etc. and now this appeal is filed on frivolous grounds.

sentences.text: 8. Onus was on the Insurance Company, to have denied the factum of accident and proved false implication.
Since they have failed to prove any of these aspects, there is no error apparent in the award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal calling for interference.
9. Appeal fails and is dismissed.
10. Let record of Claims Tribunal be sent back.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) JUDGE A.Praj.
